The first student

“I ask my guys to believe they can start over. I couldn’t ask that if I hadn’t done it myself. Same classes, same exams, same late nights.”

Ramon Clemente · First cohort student → Head of Beyond The Game

17 years of professional basketball. Then a seat in the first cohort — as a student. CompTIA certifications earned the same way he asks his cohort to earn them, a Security+ cohort now under his leadership, and the coach’s chair. This program is his own path, systematized.

Ramon Clemente · Wichita State · 17 years pro

Ramon Clemente · Wichita State

Why we exist

The call
never comes.

The career ends and nothing is waiting. No program, no handoff, no next step. The information exists and the opportunities exist. Nobody is responsible for connecting the two.

No cert. No experience. No degree in the field.

Starting over at 30 is not the same as starting at 22.

How it works

Five pillars,
Tech Employment Pathway

[ 01 ]
Direction
Assessment and one on one before enrollment. We do not place someone in a track they did not choose.
[ 02 ]
Fundamentals
Basic tech course, the same core every student clears before specializing.
[ 03 ]
Specialty
Certification in a track they chose.
[ 04 ]
Support
Coaching, community and accountability running the entire length of the program.
[ 05 ]
Outcome
Placement, Portfolio and Entrepreneurship

Advisory comes first on purpose. A skills assessment sets the technical path before a single class starts, which is what lifts completion.

Proof

The first cohort
was the proof.

Kleon Penn · First cohort

On his journey to Cloud Security

Kleon Penn is a 16-year professional basketball player from the Virgin Islands. He passed his CompTIA Tech+ exam on his first attempt, scoring 700.

First credential on the path that runs Network+, Security+, and into IT roles.

His story is published at wearebcc.org.

In the press

He retired.
Then he built the bridge.

A 17-year professional career ended.
The program started the same year.
The founder is the first proof the model.

After a 17-year professional career, Ramon Clemente decided not to enter year 18 because he felt creating this path was more important. He retired four days after Beyond Code Collective was launched.

The founder is the first proof the model works.
